name: read_little_endian_word
description: Reads the two bytes at the given address and returns them as one 16-bit value with the second byte in the high position, which is little-endian order.

name: append_string_to_buffer
description: Walks the destination string to its terminating zero byte, then copies the source string over that position including its own terminator. Returns the destination pointer.

name: format_string_into_buffer
description: Clears a 16-bit status word and stores the output buffer pointer, then passes the format string and its stack arguments to a called routine that formats them through a character callback. Writes a terminating zero at the end of the output and returns the status word.

name: copy_zero_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from the source string to the destination one at a time, including the terminating zero byte, and returns the source pointer.

name: store_selected_slot_result
description: Chooses one of two stored table pointers based on whether the argument word is 1 or 2, passes it to a called routine, and saves the returned value in a state slot. Other argument values leave the slot unchanged.

name: flush_saved_value
description: If the state slot holds a nonzero value, passes it to a called routine and then clears the slot to zero.

name: read_status_word
description: Returns the 16-bit value stored at one fixed offset in the state block.

name: forward_argument_and_saved_value
description: Passes the value saved in a state slot, together with the routine's argument, to a called routine.

name: pass_saved_value_onward
description: Passes the value saved in a state slot to a called routine and returns.

name: pass_saved_value_onward
description: Passes the value saved in a state slot to a called routine and returns.

name: record_probe_result_flag
description: Calls a routine and, if it returns zero, calls it again and stores in a flag word whether the second result is minus one, then increments a 16-bit counter in the state block.

name: reset_flag_and_bump_counter
description: Clears a flag word in the state block and increments a 16-bit counter stored at another fixed offset.

name: decode_result_with_key
description: Calls a routine and stores whether its result is minus one in a flag word, then returns the result XORed with a key byte from the state block.

name: read_key_decoded_byte_pair
description: Reads one byte through a called routine into a stack buffer, sets a flag word when the read count is not one, and returns two stack bytes each XORed with a key byte from the state block.

name: read_key_decoded_longword
description: Reads one byte through a called routine into a four-byte stack buffer, sets a flag word when the read count is not one, and returns the four stack bytes each XORed with a key byte from the state block.

name: allocate_and_store_memory
description: Calls the exec AllocMem library routine and saves the returned pointer in the state block, then calls a second library routine through a stored library base.

name: release_allocated_memory
description: Calls the exec FreeMem library routine through a stored library base to release a memory block, then calls a second library routine through the global base.

name: pass_fixed_slot_onward
description: Passes the value from one fixed slot of the state block to a called routine.

name: shift_feedback_registers
description: Advances two 32-bit state values by shifting each left one bit and adding a bit derived from XORing two flag bits of a byte, eight steps for the first value and thirteen for the second. Then calls a routine and returns its register result.

name: dispatch_changed_table_entries
description: Compares 16 state words against saved copies and, for each word that changed, saves the new value and passes a lookup-table entry selected by it to a called routine.

name: copy_table_row_to_buffer
description: Stores the index argument in two state words, copies a sixteen-byte row selected by that index from a state table into a sixteen-byte state buffer, and first calls a routine when the index's entry is empty.

name: copy_selected_table_row
description: Copies sixteen bytes from the table row chosen by a word read through a second structure into the sixteen-byte state buffer.

name: read_table_row_loop
description: Repeatedly calls a routine to read words; when a leading word is zero and a count exceeds two, reads fifteen bytes into the table row for the argument, then processes further records and returns when a trailing word is zero.

name: initialise_runtime_state_tables
description: Allocates a memory block and stores its pointer, calls library routines to set up several buffers, fills a 32-entry index table with ascending values and its companion table with minus-one sentinels, and sets twenty timing entries to 200. Returns one on success and zero if an allocation or setup call fails.

name: dispatch_index_or_free
description: For an index from minus one to seven, jumps to a routine chosen from a jump table; otherwise, if a stored pointer is set, releases it through the exec FreeMem library routine. Returns one.

name: open_library_and_device
description: Opens a library and then a device through exec and stores both pointers in the state block. Selects one of two pairs of stored values by a flag bit of the opened device and returns one; if the second open fails it closes the library and returns zero.

name: close_library_base
description: Calls the exec CloseLibrary routine twice through the same global library base pointer, with no return value.

name: allocate_two_buffer_blocks
description: Allocates two blocks through the exec AllocMem library routine, records their pointers and 8000-byte offsets in the state block, and frees the first block through FreeMem if the second allocation fails.

name: release_two_memory_blocks
description: Calls the exec FreeMem routine twice through the global library base, with no return value.

name: install_interrupt_server
description: Fills an interrupt server structure in the state block with fixed type and priority bytes, two pointers and the address of a local callback, then registers it through the exec AddIntServer library routine.

name: check_message_field_value
description: Calls two library routines through a stored library base, then calls a third on a stored structure, and returns whether a field of that structure equals the constant 1758.

name: collect_colon_terminated_names
description: Forbids multitasking, walks a linked list of nodes, and copies the name of each node of type two into a fixed buffer, appending a colon and a zero terminator for up to nine entries, then permits multitasking again.

name: check_message_threshold
description: Calls exec library routines to fetch a message and reads its fields. Returns minus one when the message type equals 82 and the difference between two of its fields is greater than 63, otherwise returns zero.

name: match_saved_names_with_patterns
description: Tries fixed name patterns through a called routine and returns the first nonzero result. It checks the saved names in turn, trying two suffix patterns for each, and returns zero when none match.

name: stub_return_only
description: Contains only a return instruction and does nothing.

name: transfer_data_in_chunks
description: Repeatedly transfers at most a fixed chunk size per call through a called routine, advancing the pointer and reducing the remaining count by the amount each call returns. It sums the transferred amounts and stops when a call returns less than it was asked for.

name: setup_named_lookups_and_buffers
description: Looks up two named entries through a called routine, falling back to alternate names when a lookup returns zero, allocates two blocks through exec AllocMem, and passes the results to further calls. Releases the second block through FreeMem when its allocation fails.

name: call_offset_routine_pair
description: Calls a routine with an offset from the base pointer and two arguments, then calls a second routine with the same offset, and then a third routine.

name: clear_field_after_two_calls
description: Calls two fixed routines and then clears a 16-bit field at one offset of a structure.

name: load_record_tables_and_init
description: Copies two groups of five longwords from two source records into split word tables, calls exec AllocMem and stores the returned value in the record, then runs a fixed sequence of library calls.

name: store_saved_value_in_record
description: Writes the saved longword from the state block into a fixed field of a record reached through two stored pointers.

name: submit_pending_update_entry
description: When a pending count is positive, zeroes a field of a record, copies five longwords from the state array entry chosen by an index into the record, and calls five exec library routines.

name: increment_counter_and_start
description: Adds one to a 16-bit counter in the state block and calls a routine when the counter reaches one.

name: decrement_counter_and_flush
description: Subtracts one from a 16-bit counter and, when it reaches zero, writes a saved longword into a record, copies five longwords from the state block into it, and calls three exec library routines.

name: set_mode_and_copy_pointer
description: Stores a mode word of zero or one in the state block, sets a global value to 130 or 136 to match, copies a saved longword from the state block, and calls a routine.

name: reset_mode_and_copy_pointer
description: Clears the mode word in the state block, sets a global value to 130, copies a saved longword from the state block, and calls a routine.

name: store_indexed_word_and_signal
description: When the first word argument is zero and differs from the stored value, saves the second word and calls an exec library routine. Stores the second word in state tables indexed by the low five bits of the first word, and calls the library routine again when the counter is positive.

name: call_stored_library_routine
description: Calls a library routine through a stored library base, with no arguments and no return value.

name: encode_offset_into_global
description: Adds 200 to the argument, shifts the result into the high byte of a 16-bit word, sets the low bit and stores the value in the global variable.

name: decode_packed_rows_to_two_buffers
description: Decodes a packed stream of literal and repeated values, using a lookup table, into a linear buffer and a second buffer with rows 320 bytes apart. It copies the finished rows to a structure array and returns when all rows are written.

name: decode_packed_rows_with_stride
description: Decodes packed run commands from a lookup table into a buffer advanced by a computed row stride, then copies the finished rows into a structure array when a flag byte is zero.

name: finish_packed_row_decode
description: Continues the packed row decoder from its saved position, writing repeated and literal values to the output and to a strided buffer, then copies finished rows into a structure array before returning.

name: resume_packed_row_decode
description: Resumes the packed row decoder at its current command position, writing repeated and literal values to the output, and returns after the last row.

name: decode_packed_literal_rows
description: Writes packed literal and repeat values from a lookup table into the output and a row-strided buffer, copying finished rows into a structure array at the end.

name: decode_packed_repeat_rows
description: Decodes packed repeat commands from a lookup table into the output buffer with 320-byte row spacing, returning after the last row is written.

name: decode_packed_run_rows
description: Writes runs of a lookup-table value into the output and the row-strided buffer, then copies finished rows into a structure array before returning.

name: copy_unmasked_rows
description: Copies rows of two longwords from a source array to a destination array. When the flag is zero it copies only rows whose mask byte is zero; otherwise it copies every row.

name: copy_rows_skipping_masked
description: Copies two-longword rows from a source to a destination with a computed stride, skipping rows whose mask byte is nonzero, for the row count given in the arguments.

name: copy_rows_unconditionally
description: Copies rows of two longwords from a source array to a destination array with a fixed stride of eighty bytes until the row counter wraps below zero.

name: initialize_decode_tables
description: Stores the argument in a global variable, then loops over all combinations of two 5-bit counters and fills four longword tables and four byte tables in the buffer with values computed from the bits of the two counters.

name: return_fixed_constant
description: Returns the constant 24576 and does nothing else.

name: double_global_and_increment
description: Doubles the global variable, adds one to it, and returns.

name: read_first_byte
description: Returns the byte at the address passed in.

name: stub_return_only
description: Contains only a return and does nothing.

name: orchestrate_six_subroutines
description: Calls six unnamed routines and is itself called by eight, with 225 instructions. Its decompiled body is unavailable, so only this call structure is recorded.

name: read_next_input_byte
description: Returns the next byte from a buffered input structure. It returns minus one at the end-of-input byte twenty-six and sets end and error flags, calling a routine to refill the buffer when it is exhausted.

name: read_next_input_byte
description: Returns the next byte from a buffered input structure. It returns minus one at the end-of-input byte twenty-six and sets end and error flags, calling a routine to refill the buffer when it is exhausted.

name: split_command_line_tokens
description: Splits a text line into up to 32 tokens at spaces, tabs and newlines, treating quoted text as one token and zero-terminating each token. Passes the token array pointer and count to a called routine, or a default pointer from the state block when the line is empty.

name: stub_undecoded_single_instruction
description: Records only a one-instruction body that was called once. The decompiler timed out, so its behaviour is not recovered.

name: uppercase_string_in_place
description: Walks a zero-terminated string and converts each byte marked as a lowercase letter in a character class table to uppercase by subtracting thirty-two. Returns the string pointer.

name: write_reversed_digit_string
description: Repeatedly calls a routine and stores each returned value as an ASCII digit until it returns zero. It then reverses the digits into the output, terminates the string with a zero byte, and returns the length.

name: format_number_as_octal
description: Converts a value to octal digit characters, reverses them into the output, terminates the output with a zero byte, and returns the digit count.

name: format_unsigned_as_octal
description: Converts an unsigned value to octal digit characters, copies them in reverse order into the buffer, terminates it with a zero byte, and returns the digit count.

name: parse_decimal_or_format_hex
description: Either formats a 16-bit value as hexadecimal digit characters, or parses a signed decimal number from a string into a 16-bit output. A stack flag selects the path, and the decompiled control flow is partly unclear.

name: format_nibbles_from_table
description: Writes a value as characters taken from a table indexed by each four-bit nibble, stores them in reverse order into the buffer, terminates the buffer with a zero byte, and returns the length.

name: parse_signed_decimal_word
description: Skips an optional sign, accumulates decimal digits into a 16-bit value, negates the result for a minus sign, stores it in the output, and returns the number of characters consumed.

name: accumulate_decimal_digits
description: Parses decimal digits from a string into a 16-bit value by multiplying the accumulator by ten and adding each digit. It negates the result for a leading minus sign and stores it in the output.

name: append_byte_to_output
description: Writes the low byte of its argument at the output pointer kept in the state block, advances that pointer, and increments a 16-bit count.

name: format_counted_into_buffer
description: Clears a 16-bit count, stores the output pointer, and passes the format string and its stack arguments to a formatting routine that writes each character through a callback. It then appends a zero terminator and returns the count.

name: store_registers_to_pointer
description: Copies the saved data and address registers and the stack argument into consecutive longword entries of the array passed in, then returns zero.

name: claim_table_slot_and_transfer
description: Searches a table of six-byte entries from index three for an unused slot, returning minus one with a failure code when none is free. Otherwise it normalises the flag argument, calls routines to transfer data according to flag bits, and stores the new state and result in the slot.

name: call_with_pointer_from_result
description: Calls a routine and, if it returns a nonzero value, calls a second routine with a pointer read from that value. Returns minus one when a state word is nonzero, otherwise returns the second result.

name: allocate_from_free_list
description: Rounds a requested byte count up to a multiple of four with a minimum of eight, then searches a free list for a block that fits and splits it when the remainder is large enough. If no block fits it requests more memory from a called routine, and it returns the block pointer or zero.

name: compute_adjusted_offset
description: Returns zero when a flag bit is set and a stored field is zero. Otherwise it obtains a value from a called routine and adjusts it by a short field of the structure, adding or subtracting it according to a flag bit, unless the routine returned minus one.

name: reset_structure_and_position
description: Sets the structure's buffer pointer to its base and clears two counters, adjusting the requested position by a short field when a mode argument is one. It then passes the position to a called routine and returns zero on success or minus one on failure.

name: read_bytes_into_buffer
description: Reads bytes from a buffered source into the output buffer in nested loops, calling a routine to refill the source when it is empty. It returns the outer loop count, and stops early when a sentinel value is read.

name: orchestrate_three_subroutines
description: Calls three unnamed routines, with 13 instructions. Its decompiled body is unavailable, so only this call structure is recorded.

name: write_fill_byte_to_buffer
description: When the counter in the structure is positive, decrements it, writes the byte in register D7 at the buffer pointer, and advances the pointer. When the counter is exhausted it calls a routine instead.

name: forward_call_result
description: Calls a routine and returns its result unchanged.

name: parse_command_and_prepare_struct
description: Reads a command string whose first character selects a mode of w, r or a and whose second character selects a sign or offset. It calls a routine for an index, then writes the index and computed flags into the structure and clears its counters. It returns the structure pointer, or zero for an unknown mode or a failed lookup.

name: read_next_buffered_byte
description: Decrements the counter in a buffer structure and returns the next byte from it. A flag bit can trigger a routine call first, and an exhausted counter calls a routine to refill the buffer.

name: flush_pending_buffer_nodes
description: Walks a linked list of structures from a fixed state offset and calls a routine for each node that has flag bit two set, flag bit four clear, and two differing short fields. It then calls a final routine.

name: forward_call_no_result
description: Calls a routine and returns, with no result.

name: call_library_recording_failure
description: If a stored pointer is set, calls a routine first. It then calls a library routine and, when that returns minus one, records an error code from another library call and sets the status word to five. The library result is returned.

name: call_library_with_offset_mode
description: Calls a library routine that returns minus one on failure, recording the error code and setting the status word to twenty-two. It then returns the argument, the argument plus the library result, or the library result again, depending on a mode argument.

name: call_library_recording_failure
description: If a stored pointer is set, calls a routine first. It then calls a library routine and, when that returns minus one, records an error code from another library call and sets the status word to five. The library result is returned.

name: check_library_result_or_fail
description: If a stored pointer is set, calls a routine first. It then calls a library routine and, when it returns zero, records an error code, sets the status word to two and returns minus one. Otherwise it returns the library result.

name: close_or_check_library_result
description: Calls a library routine and, when it returns nonzero, calls a second library routine and returns minus one. Otherwise it calls a third library routine and, if that returns zero, records an error code, sets the status word to two and returns minus one.

name: release_then_check_library_result
description: If a first library routine returns nonzero, calls two further library routines. It then calls a third library routine and, if that returns zero, records an error code, sets the status word to two and returns minus one.

name: call_library_return_zero
description: If a stored pointer is set, calls a routine first. It then calls a library routine through a stored base pointer with no arguments and returns zero.

name: compute_fixed_point_product
description: Multiplies two 32-bit fixed-point values by combining the cross products of their 16-bit halves with the product of their low halves, and returns the 32-bit fixed-point result.

name: divide_normalised_longwords
description: Divides one 32-bit value by another, using a direct divide when the divisor fits in 16 bits and shift-normalised steps otherwise. Negative operands are handled by calling a routine and negating the result.

name: normalize_fixed_point_divide
description: Divides a 32-bit dividend by a 32-bit divisor using normalised shifts and returns a 64-bit value, with the quotient in the high 32 bits and the remainder in the low 32 bits.

name: lookup_table_entry_by_index
description: Returns the address of a six-byte table entry for the index argument when the index lies within the table count and the entry is in use. Otherwise it sets an error code of nine and returns zero.

name: call_library_entry_no_args
description: Calls a library routine through a stored base pointer with no arguments and returns nothing.

name: allocate_and_append_node
description: Allocates a node through the exec AllocMem library routine, links it onto the tail of a list kept in the state block, and sets it as the head if the other list was empty. Returns a pointer just past its twelve-byte header, or zero when allocation fails.

name: call_node_routine_checked
description: Fetches a node from a called routine and returns minus one when none is available. Otherwise it calls a routine on the node's data, first calling another routine when a flag bit is set, and returns minus one if a state error is nonzero.

name: scan_formatted_input_field
description: Parses one scanf-style conversion from a format string, including an optional width and length modifier. It reads characters through a callback, handles character, decimal, octal, hexadecimal and string conversions, and stores the value through the destination pointer. It returns the position after the field, or zero on failure.

name: scan_formatted_input_directive
description: Handles a scanf-style directive using the same character class table and input callback, storing the converted value through the destination pointer. Returns the position after the directive, or zero on failure.

name: scan_formatted_input_continue
description: Continues the scanf-style directive parser at its conversion letter, using the same character class table and input callback. Returns the position after the directive, or zero on failure.

name: scan_formatted_input_entry
description: Dispatches on a scanf-style conversion letter, reading characters through a callback and storing the converted value through the destination pointer. Returns the position after the directive, or zero on failure.

name: accumulate_scanned_digits
description: Reads a run of digit characters through a callback and accumulates them into a value, then stores it and returns the advanced position. Returns zero when the first character is not a digit.

name: scan_signed_digits_into_slot
description: Reads an optional sign and then a run of digits through a callback, accumulating them and storing the value through the destination pointer, negated for a minus sign. Returns the advanced position, or zero when no digit is read.

name: scan_digits_after_first_char
description: Reads one character through a callback and then accumulates a run of digits from it, storing the value through the destination pointer. Returns the advanced position, or zero when no digit follows.

name: store_scanned_signed_value
description: Accumulates a run of digits from the input into a value, negates it when the sign word is negative, stores it through the destination pointer as a short or longword, and returns the advanced position.

name: store_scanned_short_value
description: Stores the accumulated value as a 16-bit short through the destination pointer and returns the advanced position.

name: store_scanned_word_value
description: Writes the accumulated 16-bit value through the destination pointer and returns the advanced position.

name: scan_octal_digits_into_slot
description: Accumulates a run of octal digit characters into a value and stores it through the destination pointer. Returns the advanced position, or zero when the first character is not an octal digit.

name: store_scanned_octal_value
description: Accumulates octal digits into a value, stores it through the destination pointer, and returns the advanced position.

name: store_scanned_longword_value
description: Writes the accumulated 32-bit value through the destination pointer and returns the advanced position.

name: scan_hex_digits_into_slot
description: Reads a hexadecimal number through a callback, accepting an optional zero-x prefix and accumulating the digits into a value. It stores the value through the destination pointer and returns the advanced position, or zero when the prefix is not followed by a hex digit.

name: scan_hex_digits_continue
description: Continues hexadecimal scanning from a character already read, accumulating digits into a value and storing it through the destination pointer. Returns the advanced position.

name: accumulate_hex_digit_run
description: Accumulates a run of hexadecimal digit characters into a value and stores it through the destination pointer, then returns the advanced position.

name: scan_hex_digit_value
description: Converts the first hexadecimal digit character to its value, accumulates the following hex digits, and stores the result through the destination pointer. Returns the advanced position.

name: store_scanned_result_value
description: Writes the accumulated value through the destination pointer as a longword or short, then returns the advanced position.

name: store_scanned_longword_result
description: Writes the accumulated 32-bit value through the destination pointer and returns the advanced position.

name: scan_decimal_digits_into_slot
description: Accumulates a run of decimal digits read through a callback into a value and stores it through the destination pointer. Returns the advanced position, or zero when the first character is not a digit.

name: store_decimal_run_value
description: Accumulates decimal digits read through a callback into a value, stores it through the destination pointer, and returns the advanced position.

name: copy_string_field_until_end
description: Copies characters from a callback into the destination buffer until the count is exhausted or the end marker is read. Returns the advanced position, or zero after setting the end-of-input marker in the status word.

name: check_scan_end_marker
description: When the current character is the end marker, sets the 16-bit status word to that marker and returns zero. Otherwise it returns the advanced position.

name: advance_scan_position
description: Returns the input position advanced by one.

name: copy_scanned_word_string
description: Copies characters from a callback into the destination string until a character with class bit eight is read, the count is exhausted, or the end marker is seen. It then zero-terminates the string and returns the advanced position.

name: return_zero_constant
description: Returns zero and does nothing else.

name: store_word_and_advance
description: Stores the 16-bit value through the destination pointer and returns the advanced position.

name: parse_format_specifier
description: Parses one printf-style specifier, reading flags, width, precision, length modifier and conversion letter, then fetches the matching argument. It formats character, decimal, unsigned, octal, hexadecimal, string and pointer conversions into a temporary buffer, pads the result to the field width, and sends each character through a callback. It returns the position after the specifier, or zero for an unknown conversion.

name: emit_format_string_output
description: Walks a format string, sending plain characters through a callback and collapsing doubled percent signs to one. Each percent specifier is passed to the specifier parser, and the loop returns at the terminating zero or when the parser returns zero.

name: allocate_stream_buffer
description: If a structure has no buffer or its buffer flag is set, allocates a buffer of the size stored in the state block through a called routine. It sets the buffer pointers and size fields, clears two flag bits, and records error code twelve and returns minus one when allocation fails.

name: flush_open_table_entries
description: Walks the six-byte table entries from last to first and calls a routine for each entry in use whose flag bit four is clear. It then calls a final routine with the argument.

name: call_with_register_word
description: Calls a routine with the 16-bit value in register D7 and returns.

name: release_resources_and_return
description: Calls a stored cleanup pointer when it is set, then closes a library through the global base. When a stored handle is present it calls further library routines, and it returns a 64-bit value built from the argument and a stored longword.

name: copy_c_string
description: Copies bytes from the source string to the destination until a zero byte has been copied, then returns the source pointer.

name: release_block_to_free_list
description: Returns a block of memory to a sorted free list, rounding its size up to a multiple of four with a minimum of eight. It merges the block with adjacent free blocks where they touch, and returns minus one if it overlaps an existing free block, or zero on success.

name: call_entry_routine_checked
description: Obtains an entry from a called routine and returns minus one when none is available. Otherwise it calls a routine with a pointer from that entry and returns minus one if a state error is nonzero.

name: copy_memory_block
description: Copies a block of bytes of the given count from source to destination. It copies backwards when the destination is at or above the source, so overlapping regions are handled, and forwards otherwise. A count of zero or less copies nothing.

name: allocate_sized_block_with_header
description: Frees any block held in a state slot, then allocates a block of the requested size plus a two-byte header through a called routine. It stores the size in the header and returns a pointer just past it, or zero when the size is zero or allocation fails.

name: append_record_and_process
description: Walks a linked list of records from a fixed state offset until it finds one whose field at offset eighteen is zero. If the list is exhausted it allocates and zero-fills a 24-byte record and links it onto the list, then calls a routine with the arguments and that record.

name: process_entry_and_clear_flags
description: Obtains a value from a called routine when a flag bit is set, then calls a routine with two fields of the structure when a flag mask is clear and the field is nonzero. It clears the structure's flag word, calls another routine, and returns zero only when both results succeed, otherwise minus one.

name: release_entry_if_present
description: Returns minus one when no entry is available. Otherwise, if flag bit four is clear, it calls a routine with the entry's stored value, clears the entry's word and returns minus one only if a state error is set. When flag bit four is set it clears the entry and returns zero.

name: call_exec_set_signal
description: Calls the exec SetSignal library routine. The decompiled body is unavailable, so only this library call is recorded.

name: start_program_with_command_line
description: Clears a block of roughly two thousand longwords, then stores library and interface pointers in the state block. It builds a quoted command line from a name and an argument string, and calls exec routines including AllocEntry, FreeEntry, Forbid, Permit and SetSignal before closing the library and returning.

name: find_task_and_initialise
description: Looks up a task through the exec FindTask library routine and stores its data pointers in the state block. It then calls two library routines and an empty stub before returning.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:0:02B4
name: shutdown_and_reply_message
description: Calls a stored cleanup pointer when it is set and calls two routines. When a flag word is set it calls further library routines, including Forbid, ReplyMsg and CloseLibrary, and then returns.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:0:031A
name: open_or_run_cleanup
description: Calls a library routine at a fixed offset and stores its result. If the result is nonzero it returns; otherwise it runs a cleanup sequence of stored pointers and library calls.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:0:0332
name: call_two_table_entries
description: Calls two library routines through the base register, one after the other, and returns.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:0:0344
name: stub_empty_return
description: Returns to the caller immediately without doing anything.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0000
name: select_dma_channel_mask
description: Looks up a channel record from a table using the low bits of the argument. For channel numbers below four it clears two fields of the record and stores a single-bit channel mask in a global variable.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0026
name: loop_clear_global_flag
description: Calls a routine sixteen times in a countdown loop from fifteen to zero, then clears a global flag variable.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:003C
name: start_channel_from_table_entry
description: Looks up a table entry by index and returns if it is empty. For channels zero to three it stores a single-bit channel mask in a global variable and clears the channel's fields, then fills the channel record with the entry's values and pointers, clears its counters, and calls routines.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:00BA
name: fill_channel_record_fields
description: Calls a routine and stores its returned pointer and length into a channel record, sets the record's count fields from the arguments, and when a flag byte is nonzero clears the channel's counters and calls a routine.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:00F8
name: store_channel_count_and_clear
description: Stores the count and address-derived values into a channel record, and when a flag byte is nonzero clears the channel's counters before calling a routine.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0102
name: reset_channel_fields_from_entry
description: Stores a value into a channel record, sets the channel's fields from the arguments and a table entry, clears its counters, and calls a routine when a flag byte is nonzero.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:012A
name: select_channel_entry_and_reset
description: Records a channel index and entry pointer, then either stores the entry's values from the arguments or fills the channel fields from a global table. It clears the channel's counters and calls a routine.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0146
name: load_channel_from_global_table
description: Fills a channel record's fields from a global table indexed by the argument, clears the channel's counters, and calls a routine.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0192
name: advance_channel_command_stream
description: Decrements a channel's tick counter and, when it expires, reloads it and runs commands from the channel's byte stream through a sixteen-way switch that updates volume, offsets and counters. It then stores a period value clamped to a minimum of 113 and updates the channel's position fields.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:01DA
name: advance_channel_stream_entry
description: Runs commands from a channel byte stream starting at the argument position through the same sixteen-way switch, then updates the channel's tick counters and period fields.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:01EC
name: run_channel_command_loop
description: Runs commands from a channel byte stream through the sixteen-way switch until a byte without its top bit is reached, then updates the channel's counters and period fields.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0254
name: update_channel_tick_fields
description: Stores a word in the channel's position field, advances its tick counter and, when it expires, runs the next command from the stream. It then updates the channel's volume and period fields.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:02A4
name: dispatch_channel_stream_command
description: Runs one command from the channel byte stream through the sixteen-way switch, then updates the channel's sequence position and its volume and period fields.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:02C2
name: read_channel_stream_until_command
description: Runs commands from the channel byte stream until a byte with its top bit set is reached, then stores a table pointer in the channel record and updates its position fields.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:036A
name: apply_channel_volume_and_period
description: Stores a position word in the channel record. When the channel has a pending value it adds an offset from a global table to the channel's period, and it updates a counter by a step field when that field is nonzero.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:03FA
name: enter_infinite_loop
description: Contains no work and loops forever, so it never returns to its caller.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0414
name: conditional_pointer_copy
description: When bit zero of the input is set and a stored value in the structure is nonzero, copies that value and a 16-bit field to the destination pointed to by another field. Returns the input shifted right by one bit.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0430
name: process_flagged_channel_update
description: When a global longword is nonzero, calls four routines, performs the same conditional copy as the bit-zero check, and returns the input shifted right by one bit. Otherwise it returns zero.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0698
name: step_channel_record_sequence
description: Advances a global step counter and restarts it when it reaches the stored length. For each of four channels it reads three-byte records from a data table, updates channel fields such as volume and pitch index, and dispatches the command nibble through a switch covering values zero to fifteen. It calls three routines and returns a code pointer.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:06C6
name: step_channel_records_from_entry
description: Performs the same per-channel record update as the sequence step, starting from the pointer argument and clearing the first output byte. It calls six routines and returns a code pointer.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:07A0
name: resume_channel_sequence_dispatch
description: Enters the channel sequence loop at its command handler, handling the special codes 242, 254, 253 and 255, then advances the per-channel record loop. It calls two routines and returns a code pointer when the stop code is reached.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:07AE
name: dispatch_channel_sequence_commands
description: Enters the channel sequence loop at its special-command checks for codes 254, 253 and 255, then advances the per-channel record loop. It calls three routines and returns a code pointer.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:07CC
name: advance_channel_sequence_records
description: Enters the channel sequence loop at its record-advance step, handling codes 253 and 255 before reading the next three-byte record for each channel. It calls two routines.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:07F8
name: read_channel_sequence_records
description: Enters the channel sequence loop at the record read, handling code 255 and then reading the next three-byte record for each channel and dispatching its command nibble. It calls two routines.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:080A
name: increment_sequence_global_counter
description: Increments a global counter, then runs the channel sequence loop, reading three-byte records and dispatching the command nibble for each channel. It calls one routine.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0814
name: apply_channel_effect_command
description: Applies a command effect to the current channel for command codes fourteen, twelve, nine, eight, eleven and three, then continues the channel sequence loop. It calls two routines.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0822
name: apply_channel_effect_subset
description: Applies command effects twelve, nine, eight, eleven and three to the current channel, then continues the channel sequence loop. It calls two routines.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0854
name: apply_channel_timing_commands
description: Applies command effects nine, eight, eleven and three, which set timing, nibble fields, a position value and a table pointer, then continues the channel sequence loop. It calls two routines.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0868
name: apply_channel_nibble_commands
description: Applies command effects eight, eleven and three to the current channel, then continues the channel sequence loop. It calls two routines.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0880
name: apply_channel_position_commands
description: Applies command effects eleven and three, which set a position value and a table pointer, then continues the channel sequence loop. It calls three routines.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:08A0
name: apply_channel_table_pointer_command
description: Applies command three, which stores a table pointer selected by an offset in the channel record, then continues the channel sequence loop. It calls one routine.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:08B0
name: run_channel_sequence_from_command
description: Enters the channel sequence loop at the command decode, reading three-byte records and dispatching the command nibble for each channel. It calls three routines.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:09A0
name: dispatch_channel_position_effects
description: Applies per-channel position effects from a command nibble, switching on the doubled command value. Cases adjust a 16-bit position by a delta, clamp it to a minimum of 113 and handle further effect codes before the output step. It calls three routines.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0A08
name: finish_channel_effect_dispatch
description: Updates a channel's delay field and, when its flag byte is zero, sets a bit in a global channel mask. It then applies the channel's delta to its counter, writes the result to the record and jumps through a dispatch table indexed by the command value. It calls one routine.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0C1C
name: gather_channel_command_bytes
description: Walks up to four channel records, copying a command byte from each into a register and decrementing its counter. It then applies the stored delta to the channel's position and jumps through a dispatch table. It calls two routines.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0C34
name: lookup_or_divide_table_entry
description: Looks up a 16-bit value in a global table when the index is below eleven, otherwise divides a global constant by the index. It stores the low and high bytes of the result in two global byte variables.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0C38
name: lookup_or_divide_table_entry
description: Looks up a 16-bit value in a global table when the index is below eleven, otherwise divides a global constant by the index. It stores the low and high bytes of the result in two global byte variables.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0C78
name: compute_table_cell_address
description: If a stored word is zero, stores the global buffer pointer and returns the structure's address. Otherwise it divides the argument by twelve to select a row, splits a stored longword by seven or thirty-one depending on a type value, and returns an address offset with a shift amount taken from the global table.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0C9E
name: split_cell_index_by_type
description: Divides the argument by twelve to select a table row, then splits a stored longword by seven or thirty-one depending on a type value. It returns an address offset and a shift amount taken from the global table.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0CBE
name: split_index_by_thirty_one
description: Divides the argument by thirty-one to get a row and remainder, then returns an address offset from the global table scaled by the row, together with a shift derived from the remainder.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0D18
name: scale_source_bytes_into_table
description: Multiplies sixteen source bytes by a scaling byte from the structure, shifts each product right by four and stores it in a table of global entries. It then clears a block of global words when the secondary structure is null or empty, or copies a variable-length block from it otherwise.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0D84
name: check_and_branch
description: Calls a routine and, when it returns zero, calls a second routine and returns zero. Otherwise it calls a third routine and returns minus one.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0D9E
name: call_when_flag_then_finish
description: Calls a routine only when a global flag byte is nonzero, then always calls a second routine and returns.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0DAC
name: update_global_status_flags
description: Calls a routine, then, when a global flag is set and the structure pointer argument is valid, clears the lowest bit of a flag byte. It copies a status byte from the structure into a global with bit one set or cleared, stores counters and the structure pointer, and calls a routine. It returns that call's result, or zero when nothing was done.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:21:0E18
name: clear_flag_and_call_handler
description: When a global handler pointer is set, clears the lowest bit of a flag byte, clears the handler pointer and calls the handler, returning its result. Otherwise it returns zero.
